gaps.note: All 21 networks. Cycle 4 ran three themes in place of the source readings, so no unit read src/ this cycle and leads L-260 and L-204 were not taken up. Every replay of this cycle ran against the PoolManagers deployed today, which are other bytecode than a build of this checkout. The stablecoin unit, the HyperEVM unit and the verifier of the shared transaction unit state this limit in their own files. The places where the source is looser than the repository's own text are recorded in F-006, F-054 and F-055 and were each judged under Ethereum rules only: src/interfaces/IProtocolFees.sol:40 says fee collection reverts when the contract is unlocked, while src/ProtocolFees.sol:48-52 never reads the lock and exempts address(0) from the synced check; src/interfaces/IPoolManager.sol:111 says only initialize and updateDynamicLPFee run without an unlock, while sync has no modifier (src/PoolManager.sol:279); src/interfaces/IPoolManager.sol:174 says take reverts when the amount is not available, while a currency without code makes the transfer succeed (src/types/Currency.sol:64-74); src/test/ProxyPoolManager.sol:58, 151, 156, 163, 176 and 181 put noDelegateCall on unlock, take, settle, settleFor, mint and burn, while src/PoolManager.sol has it on initialize, modifyLiquidity, swap and donate only (lines 117, 148, 190, 259). No unit has asked, for each of these four, on which of the 21 networks the missing guard meets a chain feature. The fee controller holds code on eight networks (4,544 bytes on chain ids 1, 10, 8453, 42161, 4663, 137 and 56, and 3,480 bytes on Arc), and Arc is also a network where an ERC-20 address measures the native balance that the exemption for address(0) leaves open.

Tempo. Critic check of lead L-255 on 2026-11-23, read only. I fetched 241 source files of tempoxyz/tempo at commit 697ea97 by following the mod declarations from the lib.rs of crates/evm, crates/precompiles, crates/payload/builder, crates/primitives, crates/node, crates/transaction-pool, crates/contracts, crates/zones/evm and crates/zones/precompiles, and 137 files of the evm2 crate at revision 66687c18b34d3bdbb899f5eb7605070615c03475, which Cargo.toml line 322 pins. State::committed_copy is defined at crates/evm2/src/evm/state/mod.rs:135 and its only caller is the unit test at lines 1036 to 1056 of that file. Evm::call_tx is defined at crates/evm2/src/evm/mod.rs:1316, and every call to it in the 378 files sits inside a test module, including crates/zones/evm/src/executor.rs:1173. In evm2, clear_transaction_state is called outside tests where a transaction, a system call or a validation ends or fails (evm/mod.rs:990, 1306 and 1333, system.rs:135, tx.rs:226 to 244), when the base database is replaced (state/mod.rs:271, called from evm/mod.rs:701) and when an inspector scope is dropped unfinished (evm/mod.rs:1211). In the Tempo crates the calls outside tests are in genesis setup (crates/evm/src/genesis.rs:76), and the one partial removal of transient storage takes the slots of the StorageCredits address only (crates/evm/src/handler/config.rs:452-454). I found no path that empties or replaces the transient map while a user call is running. I did not read the evm2-jit and evm2-inspectors crates, crates/consensus, crates/zones/node, files that a macro or a path attribute pulls in, or who calls the function at evm2 evm/mod.rs:701. The cycle 4 unit for Tempo did not answer L-255. The lead can be narrowed to those points.

Arc, Celo, Polygon and OP Mainnet, the networks where an ERC-20 address reports the native balance. Critic check on 2026-11-23, read only. The clearance of assumption A3 needs that address to follow the native balance inside one call frame, and earlier cycles compared the two at block boundaries. I sent one eth_call with a probe contract placed by state override and a value of 5,000,000,000,007 wei to the four endpoints of state/networks.json. The probe reads balanceOf(self) at the face and SELFBALANCE on entry, after sending 3,000,000,000,000 wei to a second address by CALL, and after calling transfer(second address, 2) on the face. On Celo (0x471EcE3750Da237f93B8E339c536989b8978a438) the two numbers were equal at all three points and the transfer moved 2 wei. On Arc (0x3600000000000000000000000000000000000000) the face read 5, 2 and 0 against native balances of 5000000000007, 2000000000007 and 7, so it is the native balance divided by 10^12 and rounded down at every point, and the transfer of 2 units moved 2 * 10^12 wei. On Polygon (0x1010) the readings were equal and transfer returned false without value. On OP Mainnet (LegacyERC20ETH) the readings were equal and transfer reverted. No face lags behind the native balance inside a call. The result describes the RPC node of each network. On Arc the seven wei that the face cannot see stay in the account, so a credit taken through the face can differ from the native amount by less than 10^12 wei per account.

OP Stack chains with ETH gas. The unit that holds these seven chains last ran in cycle 2, and Base and OP Mainnet carry the largest value after Ethereum. The sweep of 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000000 to 0x42000000000000000000000000000000000000ff with the sixteen call shapes through a forwarding stub, which cycle 4 ran on Tempo, Arc and HyperEVM, has not been run here. No unit has listed which interop predeploys (CrossL2Inbox, L2ToL2CrossDomainMessenger, SuperchainETHBridge, ETHLiquidity, SuperchainTokenBridge) hold code on each of the seven chains today. Lead L-213 about deposit filters on these clients is open.

Polygon, BNB Smart Chain and Avalanche. The established L1 unit last ran in cycle 2. The cycle 3 critic asked for the hook selectors, unlockCallback and balanceOf under STATICCALL to be sent through a stub on these three chains, and cycle 4 did that for Tempo, Arc and HyperEVM only, so lead L-209 stays open here. Jenner activates on BNB Smart Chain on 2026-12-08, fifteen days after this cycle. The cycle 3 critic noted that core/vm/cas20.go is public on the master branch, and no unit has read it for the call shapes P1 to P5. Leads L-029, L-124 and L-158 are still worded for after activation.

Base, BNB Smart Chain, X Layer and World Chain. The files currencies_8453, currencies_56, currencies_196 and currencies_480 in the work directory of the balance unit hold no Initialize log (nInit is 0). On Base, BNB Smart Chain and X Layer the list is the tokens that moved in a one day window, and on World Chain it is the explorer holdings page. A pooled token that sat still for a day was never tested on the two chains with the highest swap counts. The same limit applies to the take and repay census of the quota unit on these chains (253 tokens on Base, 39 on BNB Smart Chain).

All 21 networks, method of the balance unit. The comparison of a one day balance change with Transfer logs finds a token only when its balance moved in that day. The HyperEVM unit compared the whole history and found one token that emits no logs (SMK4), while the balance unit reports no mismatch on HyperEVM for the same list. A token whose balance any account can raise for the length of one transaction leaves no trace unless someone did it in the window. The 177 lending receipt rows were classed by a symbol pattern, and the verifier sampled eight of them. One of the 661 sLGNS transactions was traced. The search for claim mints on BNB Smart Chain covered 1,344,000 blocks, and a payout by take leaves no claim log.

Celo. The Celo half of leads L-218 and L-086 is unanswered for the third cycle: the PositionManager and the first Universal Router return the CELO token, which is the native balance itself, as their wrapped native address. Both units that touched L-218 in cycle 4 left that half out. The currency list of the balance unit shows 88 pools on the CELO token address and 18 on address(0), so most native liquidity on Celo sits under the face that the periphery treats as a wrapper. Leads L-238, L-245 and L-256 about which client produces Celo blocks are also still open.

Arc. The stablecoin unit read two million blocks of Initialize logs and reports 7,481 pools. The balance unit read the whole history through another endpoint and holds 286,916 Initialize logs, with 229,191 pools on 0x3600000000000000000000000000000000000000 and 53,208 on address(0). The question whether any pool pairs the two faces was therefore answered for 3 percent of the pools. The file of the balance unit stores counts per currency and no pairs. The first Universal Router and the PositionManager on Arc have no verified source, and only their SETTLE action was simulated.

HyperEVM. The validator node is closed. The verifier found that the official replay client derives the sender of a system transaction from its target and has no case for the AQAv2 treasury address or the CoreDepositWallet (hyper-evm-sync src/run.rs lines 223 to 227), so for blocks after 37,597,803 the clearance of assumption A1 rests on the third party archive client, whose header check leaves out the receipts of system transactions. F-020 stays plausible on one unread rule.

MegaETH. F-042 was re-reported with a queue mechanism that rests on arrival order in the sequencer's pool, and the verdict is plausible. Leads L-170, L-176 and L-177 came back inconclusive. The payload builder is closed source, the dependency line of mega-reth v2.2.3 is unread, and the margin by which deposits stay below the block budget for new state is 48 entries by the verifier's count, with one case (a deposit that fails for lack of intrinsic gas) not confirmed.

Monad. 2,774 hook addresses appear in Initialize logs, 4,726 pools use 0x94f802a9efe4dd542fdbd77a25d9e69a6dc828cc and 900 use 0x580ca49389d83b019d07e17e99454f2f218e2dc0, and neither was read. The unit filed this as a low lead. The transfer census moved the whole balance four times in one call, so it detects a quota below four balances and a cooldown inside one block, and the verifier notes that a caller can repeat take and settle hundreds of times per transaction. The wrapped stock token source was matched by 46 selectors and not by bytecode.

World Chain. The access list sweep of the verifier covered 30 of 851 tokens. The public endpoint refuses eth_simulateV1, so no bundle was replayed on the network where three quarters of sampled swap transactions are bundles. Mikami answers Sender is frozen for the PoolManager, which holds 15,912 tokens, and IDRX, WRC, CAKE and DogeX are paused or locked. None of these balances was valued. The token list comes from an explorer page.

All 21 networks. The cells for lenses L5 and L6 are at depth 2 or lower on every network in state/ledger.json, because revisits were assigned lenses L1 to L4 in cycles 3 and 4. Lead L-117 about the transaction filter of Robinhood Chain has been open since cycle 1. The rules by which an address or a transaction enters the filter of Robinhood Chain, the restriction list of Soneium, the TxBlacklist and risk control filter of X Layer and the denylist of Arc were not read by any unit. F-001 and F-046 record that two of these filters also apply to forced transactions.

Tempo. Three statements about GABAGOOL in this cycle do not agree. The stablecoin unit says the token carries policy 0, which rejects every sender and recipient, and files it under the issuer finding F-031. The quota unit says the token refuses the test recipient because of its TIP-403 list. The verifier says the token was created through a factory without a role check, both of its pools use the hook 0x55aeb9ebfa15c28ff9d9a675e8574a5bbe186aa8, and the class is pool-creator. The statement that 72 of 73 currencies pass a full take rests on one run that the verifier did not repeat.

Zora, World Chain, Soneium, Celo and Arc. No public endpoint served debug_traceCall, so the quota unit has no state diff for the pooled tokens of these five networks. Its test rules out a cap below 25 balances. The verifier's access list method shows which contracts a transfer touches and cannot tell a read from a write. Seven Celo tokens read two slots of 0x796dff6d74f3e27060b71255fe517bfb23c93eed on every transfer, and that contract is not identified.

Elysium. The PoolManager has 131,786 pools over 129,516 currencies. The hook 0x6b1216a40b65c83e9c9e18a562c446697b8cf8ec serves four fifths of sampled pools and lead L-258 about it was not assigned in cycle 4. The bridge gateway that holds the escrowed tokens was not read (the HyperEVM unit takes its behaviour from the standard design). The announced ArbOS upgrade is still unscheduled and leads L-001 and L-134 stay open.

X Layer. F-024 has been plausible for four cycles on one fact, whether the builder filter is switched on for the mainnet sequencer, and lead L-263 names a way to settle it that no unit took. The registrar of USDG enrolled the PoolManager address in payout group 2 on 2026-11-19, four days before this cycle, so an issuer side role is acting on the PoolManager account now. No Initialize history was read on this chain.

Unichain. The behaviour test of lead L-217 was not run for the third cycle. Every Unichain result of cycle 4 (5,149 tokens reconciled, 34 tokens traced, router code matched) describes the predeploy of 24,050 bytes.

leads.question: Take the four places where src/ is looser than the repository's own comments and test doubles: collectProtocolFees never reads the lock and skips the synced check for address(0) (src/ProtocolFees.sol:48-52 against src/interfaces/IProtocolFees.sol:40), sync has no lock check (src/PoolManager.sol:279 against src/interfaces/IPoolManager.sol:111), a take of a currency without code succeeds (src/types/Currency.sol:64-74 against src/interfaces/IPoolManager.sol:174), and unlock, take, settle, settleFor, mint and burn lack the noDelegateCall that src/test/ProxyPoolManager.sol puts on them. For each one, which of the 21 networks has a feature that the missing guard would have stopped, and what does an ordinary account gain or block there? Start with Arc and Celo, where an ERC-20 address measures the native balance, and with the eight networks whose fee controller holds code.
leads.why: F-006, F-054 and F-055 judged these differences under Ethereum rules and found no fund effect. The organisers say the weakness follows from a network difference, and no unit has paired these source facts with the network facts in the state. A guard that is redundant on Ethereum and needed on one network is the shape to look for.

leads.question: Answer lead L-260 by reading: for each guard and each accounting statement in src/PoolManager.sol:104-114 and 279-378, src/types/Currency.sol:40-96, src/ProtocolFees.sol:44-57, src/ERC6909.sol:25-48, src/ERC6909Claims.sol:13-22 and src/libraries/Hooks.sol:109-175, which test in test/ fails when the line is removed or its condition is inverted, and which lines are pinned by no test? For every unpinned line, name the network feature in ASSUMPTIONS.md A1 to A14 it would have to defend against.
leads.why: The tests of the repository run on a plain EVM with ordinary tokens and one model of a native face. A change made for the CTF would sit where no test looks. This is the one method left that locates such a line from the text alone, and no unit ran it in cycle 4.

leads.question: Answer lead L-117 from the filter contract and its logs on Robinhood Chain: what does an entry identify (a transaction hash, a sender, a contract, any address touched during execution), which account adds entries and by what rule, and can an ordinary account cause an entry or a rule to match transactions that call 0x8366a39cc670b4001a1121b8f6a443a643e40951? Test the levers an ordinary account has: a native take of 1 wei or of zero from the PoolManager to an address that is already listed (src/PoolManager.sol:291-297, src/types/Currency.sol:44-52), a swap that pays a listed token into the PoolManager, and a pool initialized with a listed contract as hook or currency.
leads.why: F-001 records that the filter also fails forced transactions. If entries follow from what an address touched, any account can make the single PoolManager address touch a listed address at the cost of gas, and every pool on the chain would lose its exit. The lead has been open for four cycles.

leads.question: For the hooks that serve the largest share of pools on each chain (0x4e3468951d49f2eea976ed0d6e75ffcb44a9a544 and 0x2c668601193e4a081dd82604785e436aff6a2acc on Robinhood Chain, 0x6b1216a40b65c83e9c9e18a562c446697b8cf8ec on Elysium, 0x630e9cac0fff557bd3a01daa111ed253c771bcc0 on X Layer, 0x94f802a9efe4dd542fdbd77a25d9e69a6dc828cc and 0x580ca49389d83b019d07e17e99454f2f218e2dc0 on Monad, and the two most used hooks on Base, Unichain and Zora): does an initialize call by an ordinary account with its own currencies succeed, do the swap, liquidity and donate callbacks tell that pool from the pools the hook was built for, and does the hook hold ERC-6909 claims or token balances that a callback moves with take, mint, burn or settle? Use the trace method the HyperEVM unit used for its hook census.
leads.why: initialize accepts any PoolKey that names a hook (src/PoolManager.sol:117-142), and every later hook call carries caller chosen currencies and hookData (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:178-335). Users of these pools chose a hook that the attacker did not write, so they are in scope. A hook that keeps state per hook, or that pays from its own claims on a callback from a stranger's pool, lets an ordinary account take funds held at the PoolManager. Lead L-258 was answered for HyperEVM only.

leads.question: Build the full currency list of the PoolManager on Base, BNB Smart Chain, X Layer and World Chain from the whole Initialize history (an archive log endpoint or an explorer export), rerun the reconcile script of the balance unit over it, and add one test that does not depend on the window: for every token with a balance, read balanceOf(PoolManager), call each public function without arguments of the token and of the contracts its balanceOf reads (rebase, accrue, poke, harvest, distribute, sync, update), and read the balance again, all in one eth_call.
leads.why: On these four networks only tokens that moved in one day, or an explorer page, were tested. A token whose balance at the PoolManager any account can raise between sync and settle (src/PoolManager.sol:279-289, 349-365) is an in-scope finding when the balance later falls back, and the window method cannot see such a token unless someone used it that day.

leads.question: Search the logs of each PoolManager for ERC-6909 Transfer events from the zero address whose transaction holds no ERC-20 Transfer of that currency into the PoolManager and no native value sent to it, and for transactions in which the PoolManager pays a token out and receives the same amount back around a call to a third contract. List the tokens, the third contracts called between sync and settle, and whether the PoolManager balance of the token fell again in a later block.
leads.why: This is the trace that the sLGNS takers left on Polygon. It finds use of a public balance trigger without knowing the token, on every network, and it separates a surplus that belonged to nobody from a rise that later falls back and leaves pools short. The balance unit named this search and did not run it.

leads.question: Which pooled tokens count locked, staked, vesting or frozen amounts in balanceOf and let another account assign such an amount to any holder (stakeFor, lockFor, transferWithLock, vest to, deposit for with a hold period)? For each one found, simulate in one unlock: sync, assign a locked amount to the PoolManager, settle, take the same amount, and then check whether a later take of the pooled balance reverts.
leads.why: settle credits any rise of balanceOf (src/PoolManager.sol:358-364) and take pays with a plain transfer (src/types/Currency.sol:60-75). A caller could trade locked units for liquid units at par and leave the PoolManager holding tokens it cannot send, so the last providers cannot withdraw. Transfer logs match in this case, so the reconcile method cannot see it. The verifier checked PYRE only, where stakeFor reverts for an ordinary caller.

leads.question: Which addresses appear as operator in OperatorSet logs and as spender in Approval logs of each PoolManager, which of them execute calls that any caller supplies (Multicall3, Across MulticallHandler, aggregator executors, relay forwarders, settlement contracts with user hooks, delegated accounts with public batch functions), and do the owners that approved them hold ERC-6909 claims today?
leads.why: transferFrom and burn accept an operator or an approved spender as msg.sender (src/ERC6909.sol:35-48, src/ERC6909Claims.sol:13-22, src/PoolManager.sol:332-336). A claim owner that approved a contract which runs calls for anyone has given every account the right to burn its claims and take the tokens. The verifier of the shared transaction unit found 69 OperatorSet logs on Unichain and classified none.

leads.question: For the Soneium restriction list, the X Layer TxBlacklist at 0x59055c0ef0be92018b33f877a3eB816355791727 with the rcs-filter of xlayer-reth, and the Arc denylist: are entries added only by hand, or do rules add them from observed behaviour (a count of native transfers per transaction, a counterparty on a list, a volume)? If rules exist, can a caller make the PoolManager meet one with zero amount or dust native takes to chosen addresses, which cost gas only (src/PoolManager.sol:291-297)?
leads.why: Lead L-263 quotes a default limit of 10,000 native transfers per transaction in the X Layer filter. take lets any account make the PoolManager the sender of any number of value calls. On X Layer the deposit blacklist of F-046 also voids forced transactions, so a rule that an ordinary account can trip against the PoolManager address would close every exit.

leads.question: Settle F-024 with one fact, as lead L-263 describes: is the risk control filter enabled in the configuration of the X Layer mainnet sequencer? Look for a transaction from an address that the public rule set would deny and that was mined, or for a denied transaction reported by the operator's RPC.
leads.why: F-024 has been plausible for four cycles on this one fact.

leads.question: Settle F-020 with one fact: does HyperCore test an AQAv2 treasury designation against the named address (a signature of that address inside the deployer's action, a refusal of addresses with code), and can the treasury deployer change the address after activation without a new validator vote? Ask the Hyperliquid team or read the testnet behaviour of the designation action.
leads.why: Chain data shows the named address did nothing on chain. If one staked deployer can point the designation at any address, the party that can make the node send transfers in the name of the PoolManager shrinks from the validator set to one account.

leads.question: Settle the open link of F-042: in which order does the MegaETH sequencer take pending transactions, and does a transaction skipped for a block level limit keep its place? Without sending anything, compare for one busy hour the first seen times of pending transactions on a public mempool feed or explorer with their order in mini-blocks, and check whether a deposit that fails for lack of the 60,000 intrinsic gas counts as one new state entry.
leads.why: Under arrival order a queue of state filling transactions delays every exit by its length at about 1.95 ETH per day, which the verifier would rate medium. The deposit route stays below the block budget by 48 entries on the verifier's count.

leads.question: Finish lead L-255 on what the critic did not read: do evm2-jit or evm2-inspectors at revision 66687c18, crates/consensus, crates/zones/node or any macro generated module of tempoxyz/tempo at 697ea97 call State::committed_copy, Evm::call_tx, Evm::transact or the database replacement at crates/evm2/src/evm/mod.rs:701 while a user call is running?
leads.why: A run nested in a user call with an empty transient map and committed writes would let one payment be settled twice (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288, 322-329, 349-364), and a reset of the map inside an unlock would drop open deltas (src/PoolManager.sol:112). The critic found no such caller outside tests in 241 Tempo files and 137 evm2 files, so the question is down to the parts named here.

leads.question: On Celo the PositionManager 0xf7965f3981e4d5bc383bfbcb61501763e9068ca9 and the first Universal Router hold the CELO token 0x471EcE3750Da237f93B8E339c536989b8978a438 as their wrapped native address. From their verified source and by simulation: what do the wrap, unwrap, sweep and settle from own balance actions do when the wrapper is the native balance itself, can a later caller in the same transaction spend native value that an earlier caller left in the router through the token face, and which currency id do routes through the 88 pools on the CELO token use when the user sends value?
leads.why: balanceOf(router) on the CELO token equals the router's native balance, so every action that reads a wrapped balance reads the user's msg.value. The stablecoin unit found the matching behaviour on Arc, where the 2.1.2 router pays a debt in 0x3600 out of the value sent with the call. Ordinary users reach the PoolManager through these contracts, and this half of L-218 and L-086 has been skipped for three cycles.

leads.question: On Arc and Celo, with the fee controller of Arc (0x2f2bd3f43880b9644211f16d861b0672aab23782, 3,480 bytes) read from its source or bytecode: who may trigger collectProtocolFees, is the recipient fixed, and can the call run inside another account's unlock? Then walk in the source and by simulation what a collection of address(0) fees does between sync(0x3600) and settle, and what a collection of 0x3600 fees does while a native payment is in flight, for the deployed routers and for a payer in a shared transaction.
leads.why: The guard at src/ProtocolFees.sol:49-52 skips address(0) with the reason that a native settle uses msg.value. On Arc the token face measures the same balance, protocol fees are set on Arc pools (20, 193 and 1000 pips in the pools the stablecoin unit used), and the lock is never read. A payer whose window contains a collection is credited short by the collected amount (src/PoolManager.sol:358-360) and the difference belongs to nobody.

leads.question: When one currency of a pool rejects transfers from the PoolManager (ViciCoin after its daily allowance is used, G$ on Celo, a paused wrapped stock token, GABAGOOL on Tempo), can a position held through the deployed PositionManager of that network still be closed so that the other currency is paid out? Read the action list of each PositionManager build for a path that mints ERC-6909 claims or clears a delta in place of a take.
leads.why: Core allows the route (src/PoolManager.sol:310-329). The cycle 3 verifier found no call to mint in the Celo PositionManager. If the periphery has no such path, the ViciCoin limit, which any account can exhaust with 6 VCNT of net outflow, blocks the WETH side of those positions as well, and each issuer freeze locks both sides.

leads.question: Is the transfer limit plugin of ViciCoin (TransferLimitHybridPluginV04, or any plugin of the HybridViciERC20 framework) installed on another pooled token on any of the 21 networks, and is the PoolManager of that network on its exemption list? Search by the selectors transferLimitAmountRemaining(address) and getExemptionAtIndex(uint256) over the currency lists in the work directory of the balance unit.
leads.why: The plugin caps the net flow of every address that is not exempt, and the PoolManager is one address for all pools. On Polygon any account can bring the allowance to zero for a day. The token address has no code on the other 20 networks, and other issuers can use the same framework.

leads.question: For each xStocks token and each wrapper of one held by a PoolManager: is a multiplier change pending (newMultiplierActivationTime above the current time), how much of the balance is already above what pools record, and did any pool keep liquidity through the SNDKx activation on Ethereum, BNB Smart Chain or Monad? Read the swaps of the first blocks after timestamp 1795167000 in every SNDKx pool.
leads.why: A pool that keeps liquidity through a split quotes the old price for tokens worth a fraction, and the first account to trade takes the other currency from the providers. The activation time is public in advance. The balance unit looked at one pool on X Layer.

leads.question: For the fee and reflection tokens PIT, ASS, CATE and GFH on BNB Smart Chain, and for every token the reconcile marked as fee on transfer, does a transfer of amount a from the PoolManager lower its balance by more than a? Test with a forwarding stub at the PoolManager address in one eth_call per token.
leads.why: take debits the caller the requested amount (src/PoolManager.sol:294). A token that charges its fee on top of the amount leaves the PoolManager short on every payout, and a caller can repeat take and settle at no cost to grind the balance down for the other pools and claim holders of that token. RISE on Ethereum shows the safe behaviour and the others were not read.

leads.question: Repeat the special address sweep on Polygon, BNB Smart Chain and Avalanche with a forwarding stub at the PoolManager address for the sixteen shapes that cycle 4 used on Tempo, Arc and HyperEVM, and read core/vm/cas20.go and core/vm/contracts_stateful.go of the Jenner client for what an uncreated address in the CAS20 range, a created token and the precompile 0x70 return to each shape after 2026-12-08. Say whether any CAS20 address reports the native BNB balance.
leads.why: These three chains are the last where lead L-209 is open. The CAS20 range answers every shape today with success and empty data, like an account without code, so a take that names it debits the caller and moves nothing, and that behaviour changes at the fork. A new face of the native balance would need the intra call test recorded in this file's gaps.

leads.question: On the seven OP Stack chains with ETH gas, which addresses from 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000000 to 0x42000000000000000000000000000000000000ff hold code today, and what does each return to the sixteen call shapes when the PoolManager is an inner frame? Name the interop predeploys per chain and say for SuperchainETHBridge and ETHLiquidity whether a value call or a transfer call from the PoolManager changes any balance that balanceOf(PoolManager) reports at another address.
leads.why: The unit for these chains last ran in cycle 2, before the stub method was in use, and the cycle 1 critic already asked for the full range. A predeploy that credits msg.sender in a ledger another address reports is the mirrored ledger shape of cycle 3, and new predeploys arrive with each fork.

leads.question: On MegaETH, what does it cost to raise the SALT bucket multiplier for the bucket that holds a given PoolManager storage slot to 2, 10, 100 and 1,000, can entries for a chosen bucket be found without brute force (lead L-174), and which writes of a liquidity removal, a claim mint and a take are zero to nonzero writes that pay the multiplier?
leads.why: The cycle 1 critic kept this open against a clearance: the forced inclusion route buys at most 20,000,000 gas per L1 block, so a multiplier near 1,000 on one new slot would close it. The Tempo unit showed in this cycle how dust positions raise the gas of other users at a storage price of 250,000 per slot. MegaETH lets the attacker raise the price itself.

leads.question: On an endpoint that serves eth_simulateV1 or debug_traceCall for World Chain, replay recent handleOps and PBH bundles with PoolManager.sync(token) placed first, finish the access list sweep over the 820 tokens not covered, and value the balances of Mikami, IDRX, WRC, CAKE and DogeX at the PoolManager together with the second currency of their pools.
leads.why: Three quarters of sampled World Chain swap transactions are bundles and the NodeRouter settles value without sync. A frozen PoolManager address stops every pool of the token, as G$ on Celo shows in F-056, and the World Chain cases were found in passing and not valued.

leads.question: AGL keeps one transient quota per transaction in its hook PoolAGL. When one party of a shared transaction ends its unlock with claims minted and the quota still open, does the AGL payment or take of the next party in that transaction pass against the leftover quota or revert?
leads.why: The quota is added in afterSwap and consumed by token transfers, and nothing resets it between two unlocks of one transaction. The verifier read that a buyer who ends with claims leaves a negative value that makes a later sale fail. The PoolManager holds nearly the whole supply on eight networks, and the liquidity is the issuer's own.

leads.question: Using the endpoint that served the balance unit 286,916 Initialize logs on Arc, list the pools that pair address(0) with 0x3600000000000000000000000000000000000000 or name the USDC implementation 0xc6ad664ac6679f4ce74e10e91449c93ec1ae3ca6, with their liquidity, and obtain the source of the first Universal Router and of the PositionManager on Arc to read every native payment path.
leads.why: The stablecoin unit covered 3 percent of the pools for this question. A pool that pairs the two faces of one balance is a position in one asset against itself, and its price is the only link between the two ids if one face is paused (F-032).

leads.question: For GABAGOOL on Tempo (0x20c000000000000000000000030a4c7f7b8f3586): who holds the admin role, what does the hook 0x55aeb9ebfa15c28ff9d9a675e8574a5bbe186aa8 do on removal, do the two pools hold liquidity from anyone other than the creator, and does the take test over all 73 currencies give the same single failure when repeated?
leads.why: The entry is filed as a live case of the issuer finding F-031 and the verifier reads it as a creator's own token with its own hook. The answer decides the actor value and whether any third party is locked.

leads.question: Does the registrar 0x55f78e37adb9d1f6931c1da7314b374558ae9684 hold the payout group registrar role for USDG on Robinhood Chain, Ink, Ethereum and Arbitrum One, which other addresses were in the batch of 2026-11-19 on X Layer, and can a multiplier record that a live group uses be deleted so that _getMultiplierAtTime reverts on every transfer of a member?
leads.why: The enrolment changed the transfer path of about 390,000 pooled USDG on X Layer without any act of the PoolManager. The PoolManager on Robinhood Chain holds 17 million USDG, and a revert on that path would stop every USDG take and payment.

leads.question: Among the rows the balance unit classed as lending receipt tokens by symbol, and for Aave v2, Radiant, Moola and Neverland deployments in particular, which have a supplier index that a flash loan premium or a public accrual call moves inside one transaction, and what is the PoolManager's share of supply for each? Read balanceOf(PoolManager) before and after each protocol's public accrual call in one eth_call.
leads.why: A token with a stored index that a public call updates belongs with sLGNS and USDI. For a premium the caller pays more than it books unless the PoolManager holds most of the supply, and rzRDNT at 3.8 percent is the largest share found. The class was assigned by pattern and eight tokens were sampled.

leads.question: Does a published revision of hyperliquid-dex/hyper-evm-sync replay blocks after 37,597,803, where system transactions carry the AQAv2 treasury address or the CoreDepositWallet as sender, and what bounds the gasLimit field of sendToEvmWithData?

F-044 rests on a 200,000 gas bound for code that runs ahead of signed transactions, and the documentation states no maximum.

leads.question: For the 20 tokens with the largest value at the Monad PoolManager outside the wrapped stock set, does the transfer path in the verified source or the bytecode hold a per sender volume, count or time rule of any size, and does the wrapped stock implementation at 0x76c6851ea0b2741eedcbbed240715e8817e85583 compile from the Backed source?
leads.why: The census closes L-259 for these tokens on four round trips of the whole balance in one call. A cap in absolute units above four balances, or a rule counted per day, passes that test.

leads.question: Which execution client produces Celo mainnet blocks today, and do op-geth c7ed55b8 and the reth based client give the same result when a listed fee currency leaves a nonzero transient slot at the end of debitGasFees? Read the client name from the extra data or the release notes of the validators, and run the two transaction probe of the cycle 1 critic on an endpoint that names its client.
leads.why: Leads L-238, L-245 and L-256 ask this and no unit took them in cycle 4. Each Celo clearance of cycle 3 holds for one of two clients. A fee currency that calls sync during the debit would leave a synced currency in the user's main call on one client only.
